description: The temporal half of the negation signal: the user removed an item on one run and put it back on the next. The rejection must be *superseded, not deleted* (#133) — the card retains it with status 'reversed' so the trajectory stays recoverable for policy training, but it is no longer pushed at the planner as a standing preference. A card that treated it as still active would suppress an item the user deliberately restored (the stale-memory failure #21's Knowledge-Updates eval guards against on the KG side); a card that dropped it entirely would discard a trajectory #51/#119 need.
